title: The spatiotemporal scale of an agent's goals delineates its Self (cognitive light cone)

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The spatiotemporal scale of an agent's goals delineates its Self (cognitive light cone)

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Selves can be classified and compared by the spatio-temporal scale of the goals they can represent and work toward (their 'cognitive light cone'), and this scale delineates the boundaries of each Self.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Specifically (Figure 4), a “space-time” diagram can be created where the spatio-temporal scale of any agent’s goals delineates that Self and its cognitive boundaries.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework”. Scope: Agents from microbes to humans and engineered systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.37

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A cognitive-light-cone proxy can be estimated for selected systems. Existing data cannot establish that this particular scale uniquely delineates a Self across microbes, humans, and engineered agents.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For specified agents, infer the maximum spatial range and temporal horizon over which behavior reliably reduces deviation from independently identified setpoints, then test whether these dimensions predict integration or behavioral boundaries.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The proposed boundary is a classification convention.

Cross-system datasets are not comparable.

Goals and their scales are inferred rather than directly measured.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.32
operationalizability: 0.5
data existence: 0.38
data adequacy: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Spatiotemporal scale of a homeostatic target is something an experiment could estimate for a given system. The claim uses that scale as the delineation of the Self, which is the framework's classification rule. Any measured scale is compatible with the rule, so the statement does not have a separate empirical consequence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The spatial and temporal reach of a measured setpoint can be plotted, and the claim then calls that plot the boundary of the Self.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Once goal scale is measured, identifying it with the boundary of the Self is true by the proposed diagram, with no rival outcome.
